definitions.explanation: A central virtue in Confucian ethics, representing kindness, compassion, and love toward others. One of the five Confucian virtues and a fundamental concept in East Asian moral philosophy.

examples.japanese: {仁|じん}の{心|こころ}を{持|も}つ。
{仁|じん}は{儒教|じゅきょう}の{根本|こんぽん}となる{徳|とく}だ。
examples.english: Benevolence is the foundational virtue of Confucianism.

examples.japanese: {孔子|こうし}は{弟子|でし}たちに{仁|じん}の{大切|たいせつ}さを{繰|く}り{返|かえ}し{説|と}いた。
examples.english: Confucius repeatedly taught his disciples the importance of benevolence.

notes:
One of the five Confucian virtues ({五常|ごじょう}), {仁|じん} is considered the highest and most encompassing. It represents the ideal of treating others with genuine compassion and care. In Japanese culture, this concept deeply influenced samurai ethics ({武士道|ぶしどう}) and remains a respected ideal.

THE FIVE CONFUCIAN VIRTUES ({五常|ごじょう}):
- {仁|じん}: benevolence
- {義|ぎ}: righteousness
- {礼|れい}: propriety
- {智|ち}: wisdom
- {信|しん}: faithfulness

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {仁|じん}の{心|こころ}: a benevolent heart
- {仁|じん}を{施|ほどこ}す: to bestow benevolence
- {仁愛|じんあい}: benevolent love, compassion
- {仁義|じんぎ}: benevolence and righteousness; also honor code (in yakuza contexts)
- {仁徳|じんとく}: virtuous benevolence

USAGE:
Also used as a male given name ({仁|じん} or {仁|ひとし}). Not to be confused with the suffix {人|じん} (person), which is a different character.
